description: All the text for the journey around the modules: welcome, planning the week, the practice partner, the weekly loop, coming back after a gap, and finishing. See docs/design-rationale.md for why each part exists.

welcome.title: A coach for everyday family life
body: Most parents have days when nothing seems to work. That's normal, and it doesn't mean anything is wrong with your parenting.
This coach shares a few practical skills, one week at a time, that help many families feel calmer. It's for any parent or carer of a child aged 4 to 16.
Everything you enter stays on this phone. Nobody else sees it, including us.
welcome.not_this: This is not therapy and doesn't diagnose anything. If there is violence at home, a child at risk of harm, or you're in crisis, please use Help instead.

plan_screen.intro: Here's your plan for the next four weeks. You can always revisit any module later.
plan_screen.week1_framing: Week 1 is small on purpose. A few good minutes together makes everything else easier.

setup_week.intro: Three quick choices to make this week easier. All optional.

practice_plan.title: When will you practise?
practice_plan.why: Deciding in advance exactly when you'll do something makes it much more likely you'll actually do it, especially on busy days.
practice_plan.format: If-then plan, shown back to the parent as: 'When {when}, I'll practise: {module_title}.' Ask again at the start of each new module, pre-filled with last week's answer.

partner.title: Who could do this with you?
partner.why: Having someone in on it, even just one person, helps parents keep going.

templates.co_parent: This week I'd like us to try something together: {module_title}. {short_exercise} Could we both try it, and talk on {checkin_day} about how it went?
templates.friend: I'm trying a parenting coach this month. This week's practice: {module_title}. {short_exercise} Could you ask me on {checkin_day} how it went?

partner.share_note: You choose what to send and who to send it to. The app sends nothing itself.

setup_week.reminders: See content/reminders.json. Weekly check-in is pre-selected; daily practice reminder is off by default.
setup_week.skip: Skip for now. You can set these up later in Settings.

this_week.tick_note: Tick the days you practise. It's just for you, and it fills in your check-in. Missing days is normal.

options.label: A quick refresher this week (short version)
Move on to the next module now

after_checkin.adaptation: Message and options from routing.json > weekly_adaptation.
after_checkin.repeat_preview: Next week: {module_title} again{short_suffix}. Same skill, more practice.

welcome_back.trigger: On opening the app when the check-in has been due for more than 7 days, or the app hasn't been opened for 10 days or more.
welcome_back.title: Welcome back
welcome_back.body: Life gets busy. Pick up wherever suits you.

options.label: Restart this week with the short version
Look back at a module I've done

welcome_back.never_show: Never show missed weeks, overdue counts or 'you're behind'. The plan simply resumes from where the parent is.

completion.trigger: After the check-in of the last module in the plan.
completion.title: You've finished your four weeks
completion.body: That's a real achievement. The skills keep working as you keep using them. All six modules are here whenever you want them.

options.label: Try a module I haven't done

completion.note: Finishing counts as success. Don't suggest restarting or keep prompting after 'I'm done for now'.

usage_log.description: A local, private event log so testers can choose to share how they used the app (via export). Never sent automatically.
events: setup_week_completed (with which of plan/partner/reminders were set)
usage_log.summary_view: Settings > 'My usage summary': a plain-language list (weeks started, check-ins done, days practised per week, partner shares). Included in the export file.

placeholders.short_exercise: modules.json bands[age].short_exercise (always used in shared messages, so they stay short)
placeholders.checkin_day: weekday of the parent's next check-in

quick_start.description: The fast start (docs/fast-start-v2.md): Welcome, Age, Pick a skill, then one question: when could you do it? The app plans a 3-session trial from tomorrow and a check-in the day after.

age.other_message: This coach is written for children aged 4 to 16. You're welcome to carry on with the closest age group: the ideas still apply to most families.

pick_strategy.title: Pick a skill to practise this week
pick_strategy.intro: Each one takes a few minutes a day. You can try the others later.

how.privacy_note: Calendar entries are written to look ordinary to anyone else: "Coach" and a short activity, nothing about your child. Nothing is sent from this app.

calendar_android.title: Add your reminders
calendar_android.intro: Each button opens Google Calendar with the reminder filled in. Tap Save, then come back here.
calendar_android.google_note: These buttons open Google Calendar. Only the short entry text and times go to Google in the link, as they would once saved in your calendar anyway.
calendar_android.fallback_link: Use a different calendar app? Download a calendar file instead

calendar_file.title: Add your reminders
calendar_file.intro: Open the downloaded file and choose "Add All" to put both reminders in your calendar.

trial_checkin.title: How did it go?
trial_checkin.description: The round check-in (docs/checkin-tailoring.md, section 1): result, what would make the next round easier, at most one tailoring question, then the next step from roundNextStep.

result_options.label: Did it some of the time

trial_checkin.easier_question: What would make the next round easier?
trial_checkin.easier_question_weekly: What would make next week easier?

label.4-9: Ideas for when my child pushes back
label.10-16: Ideas for when my teen pushes back

easier_options.label: It went well, I'm ready for more

trial_checkin.easier_note: Most parents adjust something after their first rounds.

messages.better_time: Finding the right moment is the hardest part. Let's try another one.
messages.not_started: Getting started is often the trickiest bit. A different time can make it easier.
messages.two_hard: Some skills fit some families better. Another one might click more easily right now.
messages.shorter: Shorter counts. A small version done often works better than a long one done rarely.
messages.pushback: Pushback is common at the start. The tips for that are at the top this round.
messages.natural: It feels odd at first for most parents. The example is at the top this round to borrow from.
messages.ready_more: Nice. A few more tries make it feel natural.
messages.ready_more_rhythm: You've got a rhythm going. A weekly plan could be a good next step.
messages.ok: Thanks. Here's a suggestion for the next round.

next_options.keep_going: Keep going: 3 more days, same time
next_options.keep_going_shorter: Keep going with the shorter version

trial_checkin.full_version_note: Show full_version_offer only for special time, ages 4–9.
